evidence.claim: Navigator truck navigation explicitly only online within Russia and Türkiye. Vehicle dimensions, actual/allowed weight, axle load are configurable. This is not Israeli restriction data.
Maps consumer truck feature has the same Russia/Türkiye limitation.

HTTP mode=truck exists; weight, axle_weight, max_weight and payload are metric tonnes; height,width,length metres. Documentation warns truck routing applies Russian Federation traffic rules; permits listed for Moscow and St Petersburg. No hazardous-goods parameter listed. Input options do not establish road-attribute export or Israel support.

Published geography Russia, select CIS and Turkey; Israel not named. Basic annual <250,000 requests table shows $1,250 and $1,625 with storage; Advanced quoted individually. These are generic prices, not an Israel truck-data offer. Paid storage/modification option is not proof of rights to build an independent restriction database.

General free terms clauses 5.1.4/5.1.5 restrict analogous services and storage/processing/modification, allowing limited performance caching up to30 days; 6.2.1 limits MapKit routing display to MapKit apps. Written commercial terms may differ (2.4); none obtained for TrucksIL.

Documented route response describes routes/legs/steps and maneuvers, not a standalone downloadable restriction inventory; no restriction match in page. This absence does not prove no private commercial data feed.
Current API examples include Dubai coordinates even for truck. This differs from product-page geography: therefore classify API Israel UNKNOWN, ask provider rather than assume universal absence.
Official Maps API feedback form is the contact channel for questions and documentation discrepancies.

Subject: TrucksIL — licensed Haifa truck-restriction pilot and data rights
Dear HERE Data Licensing Team,
We are evaluating a commercial truck-restriction database for a limited Lower Haifa pilot (WGS84 west/south/east/north 34.990,32.811,35.004,32.821). Your truck-coverage documentation lists Israel. This is an evaluation inquiry, not an order.
